mechanism.label: Lysosomal degradation (ceroid lipofuscin storage)
mechanism.summary: Cells break down worn-out parts inside lysosomes. In all NCLs this recycling fails and waste (lipofuscin) builds up, especially in nerve cells.
mechanism.description: [MOCK] Lysosomal catabolism of proteins and lipids; impairment leads to accumulation of autofluorescent storage material.

headline: One lysosomal failure, at least 6 gene names, 5 diseases in this slice
plain_summary: Every Batten disease ends in the same place — waste piling up in lysosomes — but the broken part differs. Soluble-enzyme forms (CLN2, maybe CLN5) can in principle be treated by supplying the enzyme; membrane-protein forms (CLN3, CLN6) cannot.

genes.label: CLN5
genes.summary: Makes a soluble protein that works inside the lysosome; its exact job is still being studied.

genes.label: CLN6
genes.summary: Makes a protein in the cell's endoplasmic reticulum membrane that helps deliver enzymes to lysosomes.

genes.label: CLN3
genes.summary: Makes a protein that sits in the lysosome's outer membrane.

genes.label: TPP1
genes.summary: Makes TPP1, a soluble lysosomal enzyme that breaks down small proteins. Missing in CLN2 disease.

genes.label: PPT1
genes.summary: Makes a soluble lysosomal enzyme; changes cause CLN1 disease.

genes.label: MFSD8
genes.summary: Makes a lysosomal membrane transporter; changes cause CLN7 disease.
